subject: Renewal + Dedicated expansion: warm-pool & autoscale details
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Patel <anna@bluewave.ai>, James Holt <james@cloudops.bluewave.ai>, BlueWave AI Procurement <procurement@bluewave.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + Dedicated expansion: initial ask

Hi Anna / James / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the renewal conversation last week. Per our notes, BlueWave will be renewing Dedicated for another term and is evaluating a capacity expansion to support your increased inference throughput for the recommendation API. I pulled together a quick workbook that outlines a couple of capacity options (conservative / aggressive) and the associated Reserved GPU pools, monthly committed throughput, and estimated uplift in $/token. See the attached: bluewave_capacity_workbook.xlsx.

At a high level the ask from your side was:
- Add capacity to support peak throughput of ~20k tokens/s across real-time endpoints (spiky traffic)
- Keep tail latency below 120ms p50 for 2k token sequences
- Prefer reserved pool(s) for predictable cost, but want autoscaling behavior during spikes

Two questions we need to confirm to make the renewal amendment:
1) Desired reserved pool size (approx # of GPUs) or target committed throughput
2) Commercial term change — you mentioned potentially moving from 12 to 18 months for a better rate

I'll loop in Vivek (SE) and Monica (CS) to propose a technical autoscaling profile that balances warm pool sizing, min/max replicas, and expected scale-up lag so procurement has a final SLO to review. Can you confirm your procurement timeline for executing the amendment? We aim to have a signed amendment by end of March if possible.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0119

Attachments: bluewave_capacity_workbook.xlsx

From: Anna Patel <anna@bluewave.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Holt <james@cloudops.bluewave.ai>, BlueWave AI Procurement <procurement@bluewave.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + Dedicated expansion: initial ask

Thanks Jordan — received and reviewed the workbook. A couple of clarifying items before we go to procurement:

- Can you confirm what throughput guarantees we can get once the reserved pool is added? We need a baseline SLO for sustained throughput (not just bursts).
- Autoscaling: we need details on min/max replicas, warm pool size, and expected scale-up lag. Our operations team is particularly sensitive to cold-start latency during morning ramp (we see 3x traffic in first 20 minutes).
- If we extend to 18 months, what pricing uplift vs the current term will be applied for the additional reserved GPUs?

Procurement wants to see explicit language for the amendment that covers: committed GPUs, burst behavior, and an SLA for scale-up performance. Can Vivek/Monica propose a concrete autoscale profile for us to review?

Anna Patel
Head of ML Platforms | BlueWave AI
anna@bluewave.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Patel <anna@bluewave.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal + Dedicated expansion: initial ask

Hi Anna — quick technical proposal below (I'll spell out assumptions so procurement can map to SLO language).

Summary proposal (recommended):
- Reserved pool: 8 x NVIDIA A100 (40GB) dedicated to BlueWave workload (kept warm)
- Min replicas (guaranteed running): 4 replicas (each replica == 1 GPU-backed worker)
- Warm pool: 6 pre-warmed replicas (subset of reserved pool) to eliminate cold-start overhead for expected morning ramp
- Max replicas (burst): 20 replicas (allowed burst to handle sustained spikes)
- Scale-up / provisioning lag target: 60 seconds median (95th <= 120s) when moving from warm pool to additional replicas; cold-start from zero is not included in committed SLO
- Throughput sizing: assume 500 tokens/s sustained per A100 replica for your model variant; 8 GPUs reserved -> baseline sustained throughput ~4k tokens/s with warm pool reducing tail latency and initial burst absorption; burst capacity up to ~10k tokens/s with autoscale to 20 replicas (depends on model and sequence length)

Operational notes / controls:
- Pre-warming: warm pool instances keep model weights resident and KV cache primed to recent prefixes; these are billed at reserved rate but are included in committed capacity
- Fallback: when autoscaler is saturated, requests will route to smaller quantized model variants as an optional fallback (requires opt-in)
- Canary behavior: we recommend a 2-stage rollout — canary (10% traffic) for 48 hours before enabling full warm-pool pre-warm on new model versions
- Metrics exposed: token/sec per-replica, scale events, avg scale-up latency, tail latency p99/p95, and cost burn by replica group

Attachment: proposed_amendment_BW-R9.pdf (commercial + SLO language)

If BlueWave wants to target 20k tokens/s sustained, we should plan for a larger reserved pool (16 A100s) or agree on a hybrid reserved+burst commit. Let me know the target and I can produce the final numbers.

-Vivek
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Attachments: proposed_amendment_BW-R9.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Patel <anna@bluewave.ai>, BlueWave AI Procurement <procurement@bluewave.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + Dedicated expansion: initial ask

Anna — thanks for the quick review and to Vivek for the proposal. Commercial framing here so procurement has clarity:

Option A (recommended): 8x A100 reserved pool + autoscale to 20 replicas as Vivek outlined.
- Term: 18 months (amendment to master subscription)
- Price uplift: +28% on top of current monthly committed GPU charge to cover reservation & warm-pool overhead (we can provide line-item pricing in the amendment)
- Welcome credit: Redwood will provide a one-month credit on reserved-costs for first month after amendment execution to offset migration/testing costs
- SLA inclusion: include scale-up latency target (median 60s / 95th <= 120s) and throughput accounting (tokens/sec baseline per GPU).

Next steps: 
1) Vivek/Monica to finalize SLO language in the amendment (Vivek attached a draft).
2) Legal/Finance to generate final quote and DocuSign packet. I've looped in Lauren and Marcus for sign-off on the commercial uplift and credit.
3) Anna/Procurement to confirm whether BlueWave will sign an 18-month term and whether they want the 8x or larger reserved pool (target: confirm by 2026-03-22).

If you confirm the 8x option I will ask Finance to produce a quote with the one-month credit reflected.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Anna Patel <anna@bluewave.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: BlueWave AI Procurement <procurement@bluewave.ai>, James Holt <james@cloudops.bluewave.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 14:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + Dedicated expansion: initial ask

Jordan / Vivek — thanks for the clear proposal. BlueWave confirms the following:

- We will proceed with Option A (8x A100 reserved pool) as an initial expansion, with the option to convert to 16x if early telemetry shows sustained >8k tokens/s baseline.
- We agree to the 18-month term conditioned on the inclusion of the scale-up latency SLA (median 60s / 95th <= 120s) and explicit definitions for "warm pool" behavior in the amendment.
- Procurement will need the final DocuSign and line-item quote by Tues 2026-03-23 to meet our internal approval cycle.

Please send the DocuSign link and final quote. Also include a short paragraph in the amendment that explains the warm-pool billing (how many instances billed as reserved vs billed only when active).

Anna
Head of ML Platforms | BlueWave AI
